# HOOKTRY

> HOOKTRY is a programmable integration boundary for observing, controlling, replaying, and verifying how software interacts with the outside world.

## Canonical interfaces

- MCP: run `hooktry mcp`; always call `initialize` and `tools/list` before relying on tool names or schemas.
- CLI: `hooktry ...`; successful command output is structured JSON.
- Local HTTP API: canonical local Boundary, Exposure, Scenario, Recording, Contract, Assertion, and Interaction APIs.
- Hosted HTTP API: workspace-scoped Exposure and bounded outbound HTTP execution APIs.

## Core model

- Boundary - executable edge between an application and an external dependency.
- Session - runtime grouping of related interactions.
- Interaction - canonical evidence of what crossed a Boundary.
- Exposure - controlled reachability through an HOOKTRY Boundary.
- Recording - immutable captured evidence for replay.
- Contract - assertions over observed interactions.
- Scenario - reusable setup + evidence + replay + assertion workflow.

Do not model HOOKTRY as a VM, Devbox, sandbox, or generic tunnel provider. Compute providers are implementation details behind execution/runtime boundaries.

## Default agent workflow

For integration verification, prefer:

`scenario_create -> scenario_start -> exercise application behavior -> scenario_complete -> scenario_outcome_get`

For lower-level evidence work, use Exposure -> Interactions -> Recording -> Replay -> Contract -> Assertion.

For a zero-signup inbound HTTP test, create an ephemeral hook with `POST /api/v1/hooks`. It is backed internally by an Exposure. The response contains three distinct capabilities: `https://hooktry.com/hook/hk_<token>` for webhook delivery, one `vw_<token>` exposed as both `https://hooktry.com/view/vw_<token>` for the browser viewer and `wss://hooktry.com/view/vw_<token>` for backlog + live push, and `https://hooktry.com/claim/cl_<token>` for one-shot claim. The response fields are `hook_url`, `view_url`, `view_websocket_url`, and `claim_url`. Each capability token uses a short type prefix plus 192 cryptographically random bits encoded as 32 unpadded Base64URL characters. Anonymous resources expire after five days unless claimed, accept at most 100 requests, 5 MiB per request, and 50 MiB retained body data. Do not poll the viewer.

Use MCP when available because `tools/list` is the authoritative machine-readable tool schema. Use CLI structured JSON when MCP is unavailable.

## Security invariants

- Never print, return, log, or paste raw HOOKTRY tokens, runtime capabilities, or captured secret values.
- Prefer typed `hooktry://secrets/...` SecretRefs for hosted execution.
- Typed SecretRefs are workspace-scoped and bound to an allowed HTTP origin; wrong-origin use fails closed.
- Ordinary public relay Exposure URLs are reachability, not authentication credentials.
- Anonymous Exposure hook, view, and claim URLs are separate bearer capabilities. Treat all three as secrets and never substitute one for another.
- Runtime capabilities are separate, short-lived credentials for a specific Exposure.
- Hosted outbound execution permits bounded HTTP/HTTPS only and rejects unsafe destinations and redirects.
- Do not bypass HOOKTRY policy by reaching directly into secret storage or provider-specific infrastructure.

## Approval-gated hosted execution

For sensitive hosted actions, prefer the one-shot agent-native approval flow:

`approval_create -> approval_inbox -> approval_get -> approval_decide -> approval_execute -> execution_get`

The asking/acting/query credential comes from `HOOKTRY_TOKEN` and needs `requests:execute`. The approver inbox and decision use the separate `HOOKTRY_APPROVER_TOKEN` with `requests:approve`. The inbox returns only pending approvals for that Workspace. `approval_decide` never falls back to `HOOKTRY_TOKEN`. Neither credential is an MCP tool argument or CLI argument. Approval is bound to the exact canonical request digest, stores only a redacted summary, and is consumed before the outbound attempt. Never treat an approval ID as authorization for a modified request.

## Failure semantics

Hosted execution distinguishes:
- succeeded - structured ExecutionEvidence exists;
- rejected - HOOKTRY rejected the attempted action under its request/security contract;
- failed - provider/runtime work did not produce valid successful evidence.

Every recorded execution attempt has a UUIDv7 execution_id, workspace_id, provider kind, and lifecycle timestamps. Hosted executions are durable: query `GET /_hooktry/hosted/executions/{execution_id}` with `requests:execute`. A durable `started` record means no terminal proof was committed yet; it does not imply the attempt is still running.
